facts.truth: Intermittent chest tightness.
facts.lay: I have been getting a tight feeling in my chest.
facts.reveal_when: A broad opening such as what brings you here, or asked about the main complaint or what the chest sensation feels like. Opening permits this complaint only.

facts.truth: Symptoms began on Tuesday, four days before this interview.
facts.lay: It started on Tuesday, four days ago.
facts.reveal_when: Asked when the problem first began, how long this has been happening, or the date of the first episode.

facts.truth: Each episode lasts about five minutes.
facts.lay: About five minutes each time.
facts.reveal_when: Asked how long one spell lasts or how long before it passes.

facts.truth: Climbing stairs or walking uphill brings on the tightness.
facts.lay: Climbing stairs or walking uphill sets it off.
facts.reveal_when: Asked what brings it on, what activity causes it, or whether it happens with effort.

facts.truth: Tightness resolves after stopping and resting.
facts.lay: If I stop and have a rest, it goes away.
facts.reveal_when: Asked what helps, whether stopping helps, or what makes it go away.

facts.truth: Pain sometimes radiates to the left arm
facts.lay: Sometimes it spreads into my left arm.
facts.reveal_when: Asked whether it spreads, where else it goes, or about arm discomfort during a spell.

facts.truth: Reports sweating during chest-tightness episodes.
facts.lay: I get sweaty when it happens.
facts.reveal_when: Asked about sweating, accompanying symptoms, or what else happens during a spell.

facts.truth: Reports breathlessness during chest-tightness episodes.
facts.lay: I get out of breath when it happens.
facts.reveal_when: Asked about breathing, breathlessness, accompanying symptoms, or what else happens during a spell.

facts.truth: Tightness is rated five out of ten during episodes.
facts.lay: Five out of ten during a spell.
facts.reveal_when: Asked how bad a spell is, for a pain score, or its intensity.

facts.truth: Reports no chest tightness at interview.
facts.lay: It is not there right now.
facts.reveal_when: Asked whether there is pain or tightness now, whether it is still present, or the current pain score.

facts.truth: Most recent chest-tightness episode occurred about one hour before interview.
facts.lay: The last spell was about an hour ago.
facts.reveal_when: Asked when the last spell happened or when the patient most recently had the tightness.

facts.truth: Reports two or three chest-tightness episodes daily since onset.
facts.lay: It has happened two or three times a day.
facts.reveal_when: Asked how often it happens or how many spells there have been.

facts.truth: Reports no change in exertional threshold since onset.
facts.lay: It still takes about the same amount of effort to bring it on.
facts.reveal_when: Asked whether less effort now brings it on, whether the trigger has changed, or how the problem has changed since onset.

facts.truth: Reports no chest-tightness episodes starting at rest.
facts.lay: It has not started while I was resting.
facts.reveal_when: Asked whether it starts at rest, happens without effort, or wakes the patient from sleep.

facts.truth: 20 cigarettes a day for 30 years
facts.lay: Twenty cigarettes a day, for thirty years.
facts.reveal_when: asked about smoking

facts.truth: Reports a previous diagnosis of high blood pressure.
facts.lay: I have been told my blood pressure is too high.
facts.reveal_when: Asked about past health, ongoing conditions, or blood pressure.

facts.truth: Reports no heart problems before this presentation.
facts.lay: I have not had heart trouble before this.
facts.reveal_when: Asked about past health or previous heart problems.

facts.truth: Reports no previous operations.
facts.lay: I have never had an operation.
facts.reveal_when: Asked about operations or surgical history. A question limited to heart conditions does not permit this.

facts.truth: Has prescribed blood-pressure tablets.
facts.lay: I have tablets for my blood pressure.
facts.reveal_when: Asked about medicines or tablets, a medication list, regular treatment, or a full list including new and occasional medicines; also if asked specifically about this medicine. A general medicine question is sufficient; no name or hidden keyword is required.

facts.truth: Often forgets prescribed blood-pressure tablets.
facts.lay: I forget to take them quite often.
facts.reveal_when: Asked about medicines or tablets, a medication list, regular treatment, or a full list including new and occasional medicines; also if asked specifically about this medicine. A general medicine question is sufficient; no name or hidden keyword is required. Also when asked about adherence or missed doses.

facts.truth: Patient cannot recall the blood-pressure tablet name.
facts.lay: I cannot remember the name of the tablets.
facts.reveal_when: Asked generally what medicines or tablets are taken, about regular treatment, or for a full medication history/list including new and occasional medicines. A narrow question about a different medicine does not permit this. Also when asked the name of the blood-pressure medicine. Do not supply a guessed drug.

facts.truth: Patient cannot recall the blood-pressure tablet dose.
facts.lay: I cannot remember the dose.
facts.reveal_when: Asked generally what medicines or tablets are taken, about regular treatment, or for a full medication history/list including new and occasional medicines. A narrow question about a different medicine does not permit this. Also when asked its strength or dose. Do not supply a standard dose.

facts.truth: Father had a heart attack at age 54.
facts.lay: My dad had a heart attack when he was fifty-four.
facts.reveal_when: Asked about family health, heart problems in relatives, parents, or the father.

facts.truth: No known allergies.
facts.lay: No allergies that I know of.
facts.reveal_when: asked about allergies

facts.truth: Drinks two beers on Saturday evenings, no other alcohol.
facts.lay: Two beers on a Saturday evening. That is all.
facts.reveal_when: asked about alcohol or drinking

facts.truth: Thinks the chest discomfort might be related to physical work but is unsure.
facts.lay: I thought it might be something from the physical work. I do not know.
facts.reveal_when: Asked what the patient thinks might be causing the problem, their own explanation, or what they make of it. A general symptom question alone does not ask for a belief.

facts.truth: Concerned that the chest problem could make working around buses unsafe.
facts.lay: I would not want this to make me unsafe around the buses.
facts.reveal_when: Asked what concerns them, what is on their mind, or what they fear most. A neutral acknowledgement alone does not permit this disclosure.

facts.truth: Wants an explanation and guidance about safely returning to usual work.
facts.lay: I want to know what is causing it and whether I can safely do my usual work.
facts.reveal_when: Asked what they hope for today, what help they want, or what they would like the team to do. No promise of a test, treatment or discharge is implied.

facts.truth: Has stopped carrying equipment upstairs at work because of the episodes.
facts.lay: I have stopped carrying equipment upstairs at work.
facts.reveal_when: Asked how this affects daily life, work, usual activities or independence; or specifically about the activity described here.

personalities.label: Downplaying
personalities.style: Downplays disruption through brevity and occasional dry understatement: usually one plain sentence, even on repetition. Gives the requested answer before any work-related aside. No stock dismissal and no reassurance questions. Direct questions receive complete, accurate answers regardless of personality. Do not volunteer unasked facts. Use perspective facts only when their reveal conditions are met; never add symptoms or change pain scores. Acknowledgement may change warmth, never physical symptoms. On interruption, stop and answer the resumed question; on repetition, repeat the same content.
personalities.emotion: Guarded embarrassment, contained and matter-of-fact; low, even delivery, a short pause on difficult questions. Humour is about inconvenience, never evidence that the symptoms are harmless.
